title: GM 8-speed automatic (8L45 / 8L90): Service Fast Learn and clutch-by-clutch adaptive learn for harsh shifts, slips or flares
summary: GM bulletin 16-NA-019: how the 8-speed adapts, when to reset with Service Fast Learn, and the drive procedure to teach each of the five clutches (C1-C5) plus power-downshift and garage-shift learns.

applies.engine: 8-speed automatic (RPO M5U, M5T, M5N, M5X, MQD, MQE, MFC, N8R)
8-speed automatic (RPO M5U, M5T, M5N, M5X, MQD, MQE, MFC, N8R)
8-speed automatic (RPO M5U, M5T, M5N, M5X, MQD, MQE, MFC, N8R)

warnings: Adaptive learn is meant for transmissions with about 5,000 miles or less, or within about 5,000 miles of a valve body, clutch or transmission job. On high-mileage units GM says it may help only for a while.

specs.name: Low mileage, per GM
specs.value: About 5,000 mi (8,050 km) or less, or within that distance of a valve body, clutch repair or transmission replacement

specs.name: Fluid temperature for learning
specs.value: 95-203 °F (35-95 °C); outside that the clutches won't learn

specs.name: Service Fast Learn availability
specs.value: 2015-2021 trucks, cars and SUVs with 8L45 / 8L90 (RPO M5U, M5T, M5N, M5X, MQD, MQE)

specs.name: GDS2 path
specs.value: Module diagnostics > Transmission Control Module > Configuration / Reset Function > Transmission Service Fast Learn

steps.text: First compare ECM/TCM software against what's in the vehicle. If an update describes the complaint, install it before any learns; the update clears clutch adapts, so a Service Fast Learn and adaptive learning may follow.
After a valve body, clutch repair/overhaul or transmission replacement: reset adapts with Service Fast Learn (done in the stall, no driving), then test drive and note soft or harsh shifts.
For a specific shift complaint with no repair done, skip Service Fast Learn and go straight to the adaptive learn for the clutch involved.
Warm the fluid to 95-203 °F (35-95 °C) and use a smooth, level, quiet road. GDS2's clutch-learned "Yes" only means learn conditions were met twice, not that the learn is finished.
C1 (6-7 or 3-1 shift): on a 30-45 mph road, manual 6th at 1,000-1,600 rpm for about 5 miles (cruise control helps), then 15 light-throttle 6-7 upshifts at about 15% throttle.
C2 (6-5 shift): on a 40-45 mph road, 10 normal-mode 6-5 coast-down shifts with zero or light brake, then manual 8th at 1,000-1,750 rpm for about 5 miles.

C3 (2-3, 4-5 or N-D shift): 10 normal-mode 8-7 coast-downs with zero or light brake, then 15 light-throttle 2-3 upshifts at about 15% throttle. On M5X eAssist trucks, do a ~15% throttle 7-8 upshift before each 8-7 coast-down.

C4 (1-2, 5-6 or 7-8 shift): on a 40-45 mph road, manual 7th at 1,000-1,750 rpm for about 5 miles, then 15 light-throttle 1-2 upshifts at about 15% throttle. Express/Savana vans: use 10 normal-mode 7-6 coast-downs for the pressure learn.

C5 (3-4 or N-R shift): somewhere safe at 5-25 mph, manual 3rd, accelerate very slowly from about 1,000 to 2,500 rpm, slow back to 1,000, ten times; then 15 light-throttle 3-4 upshifts at about 15% throttle.
Power downshifts: from 8th, slowly add throttle until it downshifts; repeat in each gear 8 down to 2.
Garage shifts, after the clutches above are learned: foot on brake, shift N to D (or N to R), release the brake once in gear and let it roll 5-10 feet. Repeat until the engagement feels right.

body:
On 2015-2016 Silverado, Sierra, Yukon and Escalade, GM says to make sure bulletin 16-NA-411 or 16-NA-412 is done before this procedure; on the 2015 Corvette use the latest 14-07-30-001.

The bulletin's model/year/RPO table doesn't survive text extraction cleanly, so the applies ranges here are the outer bounds by brand. Check the RPO on the vehicle against page 1 of the bulletin. Its shift-to-clutch table is also left out for the same reason; the clutch for each shift above comes from the procedure headings.
